'''''Notobasis syriaca''''', or the '''Syrian thistle''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is a species of flowering plant in the tribe [[Cardueae]] within the family [[Asteraceae]]. It is native to the [[Mediterranean region]] and the [[Middle East]], from [[Madeira]], the [[Canary Islands]], [[Morocco]] and [[Portugal]] east to [[Egypt]], [[Iran]] and [[Azerbaijan]].

It is an [[annual plant]] belonging to the semi-desert flora, growing to 30–100 cm tall. The [[leaf|leaves]] are spirally arranged on the stems, deeply lobed, grey-green with white veins, and sharp spines on the margins and apex. The [[flower]]s are purple, produced in a dense [[inflorescence|flowerhead]] (capitulum) 2 cm diameter, surrounded by several spiny basal bracts.<ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/floraspecie.php?genere=Notobasis Altervista Flora Italiana, genere ''Notobasis''] includes photos and distribution maps</ref>

In the [[Greece|Greek]] island of [[Crete]], where it is called agavanos <big>(αγκάβανος),</big> its tender shoots are peeled and eaten raw by the local people.

It is [[naturalisation (biology)|naturalised]] in [[Australia]].
